get.summary: One kind's items with their translation into one language
get.description: What the Translations screen lists: a page of the store's products, categories or collections, ordered by title, each with its own text beside its translation into `language`, and how many of the store's items that language covers.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What is being translated: `product` (title, description, seo_title, seo_description), `category` (title) or `collection` (title, description) — the kinds and fields the engine applies on the storefront's reads. Accepting `variant` would store rows nothing reads.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: One of the store's languages other than its main one, as a BCP 47 tag: the main language's text is the item's own, and a language the store does not sell in is never served (D87).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches anywhere in the item's own title, case-insensitively.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only the items with no translation into language yet, or only the ones with one.

get.description: Ordered by language, so a picker renders the same way twice. An item nobody has translated answers an empty list rather than null.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What is being translated: `product` (title, description, seo_title, seo_description), `category` (title) or `collection` (title, description) — the kinds and fields the engine applies on the storefront's reads. Accepting `variant` would store rows nothing reads.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The product's, category's or collection's id.

put.summary: Write one item's translation into one language
put.description: Replaces the whole field set rather than merging it, like every other whole-object PUT here: the caller sent the translation it wants, and a merge would make removing a field impossible. Emptying every field is the same intention as deleting the row, and answers 204 — an empty object left behind would show up as a language this item claims to be translated into.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What is being translated: `product` (title, description, seo_title, seo_description), `category` (title) or `collection` (title, description) — the kinds and fields the engine applies on the storefront's reads. Accepting `variant` would store rows nothing reads.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The product's, category's or collection's id.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: One of the store's languages other than its main one, as a BCP 47 tag: the main language's text is the item's own, and a language the store does not sell in is never served (D87). A regional tag falls back to its primary subtag on read, so a row stored for `fr` serves a shopper asking for `fr-CA`, and an exact `fr-CA` row beats it.

204.description: Every field was empty, so the translation was removed.

delete.summary: Remove one item's translation into one language
delete.description: 204 whether or not a row went: deleting a translation that is not there leaves the world in the state the caller asked for.

fields.description: The translated fields, from the kind's own list — an unknown name is refused rather than dropped, because a silently discarded field is a translation somebody believes they wrote. A field left out keeps the item's stored text rather than blanking it.
The kind's translatable fields, in the order a form shows them.

path.description: Where a category sits, such as "Jewellery / Rings". Absent for products and collections.

original.description: The store's own text, in its main language, one entry per field.

translation.description: The translation into language, or null until somebody writes one.

matching.description: How many items the search and the status filter match: what the page is a page of.

total.description: How many items of this kind the store has. Archived products are left out of every count and list.

translated.description: How many of them have a translation into language.
